source.title: Conditional Co-Ablation: Recovering Self-Repair Backups in Transformer Circuits
source.authors: Z. Gong; Heng-Yang Lu; Tian-Tong Wang; Yi-Chi Zhang; Yi-Xin Wang; Zi-Hao Zeng; Ming-Gan Xiao; Chau Yuen; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests IOI backup recruitment and circuit completeness using conditional co-ablation and freezing interventions, rather than the original circuit-finding recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports backup-recovery AUCs, causal freezing effects, circuit incompleteness, and robustness tests. It also reports results for induction circuits in other models; those test a different behavior from IOI and are listed under fits_no_version. Values used to select calibration settings or matched primary sets are not treated as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly about a method: CoAx ranks heads by how much their ablation effect grows after a given primary set is removed. Its IOI experiments still measure backup name-mover self-repair directly. After the three primary name-movers are removed, the backup branch's direct IO−S attribution roughly triples. The IO−S margin falls only from 2.57 to 2.29. Freezing the documented backups costs 0.57 margin. Primaries and backups together are strongly non-additive. These results bear on V2. Two alternative templates give a weak test of V6. Most other rows score the method's own ranking against the original paper's backup labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that self-repair makes intact-state circuits incomplete under intervention. On GPT-2-small IOI, conditioning on primary name-mover removal exposes the documented dormant backups, which causally carry repair. Adding CoAx-selected heads reduces circuit incompleteness from 0.47 to 0.24. The approach extends to repair across mechanisms and to induction-circuit completion in 8 other models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses finite conditional co-ablation and freezing after removal of a supplied primary set, rather than reproducing the original circuit-discovery and faithfulness/completeness/minimality procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Backup ranking varies with the identity of the removed primary set and the output geometry; the reported Fisher score is 0.941 AUC versus 0.905 with plain ℓ2. CoAx recovery remains between 0.941 and 0.974 across four ablation operators, and is 0.94, 0.93, and 0.92 on the standard and two alternative templates. The main result is reported across four prompt seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: CoAx completions of detected induction circuits beat size-matched random completions on all 8 non-GPT-2 models, with a family-macro gain of 6.70.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conditional co-ablation finds heads that complete induction circuits across model families.

fits_no_version.finding: CoAx head rankings recover the documented IOI backups better than intact-state attribution. Recovery is robust to ablation operator and calibration size, and specific to the removed primary set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Comparing ablation effects before and after primary-set removal identifies dormant backups better than intact-state attribution.

fits_no_version.finding: CoAx growth agrees positively with freeze-based repair in 11 of 12 held-out instances across name-mover, S-inhibition, induction and duplicate-token clusters (macro Spearman +0.123).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conditional effect growth predicts which heads carry repair across mechanisms.

record.problems: Documented backup labels are available only for GPT-2-small IOI. The authors state that automatically identifying the primary set is a separate problem. Some robustness outcomes are reported without uncertainty estimates, and the cross-model extension concerns induction rather than IOI.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was not reached. Not every auxiliary comparator, backup-label metric, alternative primary-set condition, or robustness analysis was entered as a separate row; the main recovery result, key controls, causal tests, circuit-completion results, ablation-operator checks, prompt-template checks, and cross-model induction results are represented.

untested.parts: The study takes the 26-head, 7-class circuit as given. It does not re-test faithfulness, completeness or minimality of that circuit.
The other models are tested only on induction circuits. No other model, size or checkpoint is tested for an IOI circuit.
No comparison of other circuit-finding methods recovering the full IOI circuit.
The ablation-operator and metric variations apply to the CoAx ranking, not to the circuit's faithfulness or completeness.
Name-order variants (ABBA/BABA) and prompts with more names are not tested. The templates are tested only through backup-label recovery.

missing.what: Other 133 heads' IO−S attribution shifts from −0.773 to +0.392 after primary removal
Non-additivity: the joint primary-plus-backup ablation drops the margin by 1.30, against 0.67 for summed single-head effects (1.9×); primaries alone drop it by 0.28
Graded wake-up and dose response: backup output-norm ratio rises from 1.00 to 1.15 as primaries are removed, while random heads stay flat
Documented backup [10,6] direct IO−S contribution rises from +0.07 to +0.21 after primary removal
The 'documented circuit' has incompleteness D=0.300±0.027 in response to primary removal. Which heads it contains is not clearly stated, so the bearing on V5 cannot be determined.

record.verdict_notes: This is mainly a method paper that uses the original paper's backup labels as ground truth, so most rows are method performance and were set to none. The V2 evidence is the hand-off, freezing and non-additivity measurements. The V5 rows in the record concerned ablation sensitivity of the method's ranking, not of circuit faithfulness, so no V5 verdict is given. The cross-model results concern induction, not IOI, so V3 is untested.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not re-establish all 26 heads, all 7 classes and their roles, or the original faithfulness and minimality criteria across the intact-model IOI behavior.
The study tests recruitment and causal load-bearingness for documented and selected backup heads under primary name-mover removal, not every possible ablation or backup configuration.
The cross-model experiments concern induction behavior, not IOI circuits or reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
The study compares estimators and controls but does not test whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, and metrics recover essentially the same full IOI circuit.
The study does not comprehensively vary prompt distributions or assess all faithfulness and minimality metrics from the original claim.
The study tests two alternative IOI templates, but not different name orders or prompts with more names.

relationships.condition: GPT-2-small IOI, zero ablation of the three primary name-movers
relationships.reason: The backup branch's IO−S attribution rises from +0.57 to +1.68 and the margin falls only from 2.57 to 2.29. Freezing the backups costs 0.57 margin, and documented backups show the most effect growth (R1, R10, R12, R13). CoAx-selected heads also carry repair (R11).
relationships.display_finding: Backup IO−S attribution rose from +0.57 to +1.68 while the margin fell from 2.57 to 2.29; freezing backups cost 0.57 margin, documented backups showed the greatest effect growth, and CoAx-selected heads also contributed to repair.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: GPT-2-small IOI, zero ablation of the three primary name-movers
source_check.reason: R10, R12 and R13 establish increased backup name-moving contribution, a largely preserved IOI margin and a causal freezing cost; R11 establishes load-bearingness of the selected set.

relationships.condition: Distribution of compensation after primary removal
relationships.reason: The documented backups replace only part of the lost +2.52 primary contribution (+1.68; R12). The text reports that the other 133 heads shift from −0.77 to +0.39. Other selected sets carry more repair when frozen (co-activation 1.97 vs documented 0.57). Repair is therefore not confined to the eight documented backups; the 133-head shift and the co-activation figure come from the text, not from rows.
relationships.display_finding: Documented backups contributed +1.68 against a lost +2.52 primary contribution, while the other 133 heads shifted from −0.77 to +0.39; freezing co-activation-selected heads cost 1.97 margin versus 0.57 for the eight documented backups.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Distribution of compensation after primary removal
source_check.reason: V2 does not require complete replacement by the eight documented backups or exclude compensation by other heads. R12 and the remaining-head attribution shift support distributed compensation. Section C.3.4 explicitly warns that freezing magnitudes are not partitions of total repair.

relationships.reason: Documented backups are recovered at AUC 0.93 and 0.92 against 0.94 on the standard template. This indirectly suggests the same backup heads respond across these templates (R20-R22).
relationships.display_finding: Documented backups were recovered at AUC 0.93 and 0.92 on the alternative templates, compared with 0.94 on the standard template.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. The remaining 133 heads shift from −0.773 ± 0.151 to +0.392 ± 0.141; freezing losses must not be interpreted as additive shares of repair. Aggregate synthesis counts were outside this single-study check.

statements.correction: Primary contribution intact: +2.519 ± 0.169; backup contribution intact: +0.567 ± 0.048; backup contribution after removal: +1.680 ± 0.149. Freeze losses: CoAx 0.90 ± 0.07; documented backups 0.57 ± 0.09. These losses measure load-bearingness, not partitions of total repair.
statements.problem: The facts are accurate, but they do not establish a limitation of V2: V2 requires neither complete replacement by the documented eight backups nor compensation confined to those heads.
